explanation: The Urals run from the Arctic coast south towards Kazakhstan, splitting Russia into a European west and an Asian east. They are old, worn mountains, far lower than the Alps.

claims.text: The Ural Mountains are usually taken as part of the boundary between Europe and Asia.
The Carpathians, the Alps and the Altai Mountains are not used as the boundary between Europe and Asia.
The Ural Mountains run roughly north to south from the Arctic coast towards Kazakhstan.
The Urals divide Russia into a European part to the west and an Asian part to the east.
The Ural Mountains are old and worn down, and far lower than the Alps.

evidence.restatement: The Urals are the conventional Europe-Asia boundary in Russia.
The Carpathians and the Alps lie inside Europe and the Altai inside Asia; none is used as the boundary.
The Urals run north-south from the Arctic coast towards north-west Kazakhstan.
Russia west of the Urals is counted as European and east of them as Asian.
The Urals are an old, eroded range, topping out under 1,900 m against the Alps' 4,800 m.
